author: Vox
description:
The Lindsay Clancy trial has captivated the nation for weeks now. Breakdowns of the case — and conspiracy theories, too — have saturated social media, with people searching for answers to questions like: How could a suburban mother kill her three children? Was the husband, Patrick Clancy, involved somehow? What can we all do to prevent this from happening to our loved ones or even us? 

While some content creators are cautious about being ethical and sticking to the facts, others indulge in conspiracies or crime-solving narratives that enter a sticky ethical gray area. It all points to our fascination with true crime, and how we use these stories to bring larger societal issues to light. 

Crime historian and podcaster Kate Winkler Dawson and true crime content creator Haley Price share their experiences working in the world of true crime — and why it’s important to remember that at the center of these stories are real people.

author: Vox
description:
Have you noticed the bad vibes around dating lately? Whether you’re swiping on apps or scrolling through social media, it’s easy to feel like the romantic landscape has become a battleground — at least, for the heterosexual among us. This pervasive feeling of hopelessness and negativity — often called "hetero-pessimism" — is everywhere. But is this cynicism the actual picture, or is it just another digital trap?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode of The Gray Area, host Jonquilyn Hill is joined by Magdalene J. Taylor, senior editor at Playboy. Together, they dissect why we’ve become so hostile towards straight dating, the disconnect between our online expectations and real-world reality, and why Magdalene is making a radical case for "hetero optimism."
